The European Court of Human Rights held, by 9 votes to 8 in the Grand Chamber, that the UK did not violate Article 6(1) when its courts barred Mr Al-Adsani's torture damages claim against Kuwait on state immunity grounds. The Court found that the immunity pursued a legitimate aim and was proportionate, so in this case immunity prevailed over the fair-trial right. The Court rejected the idea that human rights override most immunities, so the second option in the team note fits the outcome better than the first.

CONFIDENCE: 85
